verses.text: Theophilus, in my first book I wrote about all that Jesus began to do and to teach,
until the day he was taken up to heaven. Before that, through the Holy Spirit, he gave orders to the apostles he had chosen.
After he suffered, he showed himself to them alive, and gave many proofs. He appeared to them over forty days and spoke about God's Kingdom.
While he was with them, he gave them this order: "Do not leave Jerusalem. Wait for what the Father promised, which you heard about from me.
John baptised with water, but in a few days you will be baptised with the Holy Spirit."
When they had come together, they asked him, "Lord, is this the time you will give the kingdom back to Israel?"
He said to them, "It is not for you to know the times or dates that the Father has set by his own authority.
But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you. You will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth."
After he said this, he was taken up while they watched, and a cloud hid him from their sight.
They were still staring into the sky as he went, when suddenly two men dressed in white stood beside them.
They said, "Men of Galilee, why do you stand here looking into the sky? This same Jesus, who has been taken from you into heaven, will come back in the same way you saw him go."
Then they went back to Jerusalem from the hill called the Mount of Olives. It is near Jerusalem, about a kilometre away.

When they arrived, they went up to the upstairs room where they were staying. Peter, John, James, Andrew, Philip, Thomas, Bartholomew, Matthew, James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, and Judas son of James were there.
They all kept praying together with one mind. The women were with them, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and his brothers.
In those days Peter stood up among the believers, a group of about one hundred and twenty people, and said,
"Brothers, the Scripture had to come true which the Holy Spirit spoke long ago through David. It was about Judas, who led the men who arrested Jesus.
He was one of us, and he had a share in this work."
Judas bought a field with the money he was paid for his evil act. There he fell head first, his body burst open, and all his insides poured out.
Everyone living in Jerusalem heard about this. So in their language they called that field Akeldama, which means Field of Blood.
Peter said, "It is written in the book of Psalms, 'Let his home become empty. Let no one live in it.' And also, 'Let someone else take his place of leadership.'
"So we must choose one of the men who have been with us the whole time the Lord Jesus lived among us,
from the time John baptised him until the day he was taken up from us. One of these must join us as a witness that Jesus rose from the dead."
They put forward two men: Joseph called Barsabbas, who was also known as Justus, and Matthias.
Then they prayed, "Lord, you know everyone's heart. Show us which of these two you have chosen
to take over this work as an apostle, which Judas left to go where he belongs."
Then they drew lots, and the lot fell to Matthias. So he was added to the eleven apostles.
